sentences.text: Opposite Party
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Pradeep Kumar Srivastava

For the Petitioner : Mr. Pran Pranay, Adv.
 : Mr. Kehkashan Afsheen

For the State : Mr. Pankaj Kumar, A.P.P.
 Order No.04 /Dated- 15.07.2024
 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. The petitioner has been made accused in connection with Jamtara Cyber P.S. Case No. 15 of 2024,
registered for the offence under Sections 414, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120B of Ipc and under
Sections 66(B), 66(C), 66(D) of the I.T. Act, pending in the Court of learned Additional Sessions
Judge-I, Jamtara.
3.  As per FIR, informant received secret information that some people were committing cybercrime.

To verify the same, informant along with raiding party reached at the house of co-accused, Sagar Mandal and apprehended two accused person including present petitioner and from their possession some mobile phones along with SIM Cards were recovered and seized.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all as alleged in this case.
Petitioner has no criminal antecedent.
Petitioner is in judicial custody since 05.03.2024.
Other co-accused persons have been granted bail by the Co-Ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 20th June, 2024 in B.A. No. 3292 of 2024, B.A. No. 3354 of 2024 and B.A. No. 3355 of 2024.

Petitioner undertakes to cooperate in the trial of the case by remaining physically present as and when required and shall not indulge in any manner in tampering with the prosecution evidences or influencing the witnesses of prosecution.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of bail.
5. On the other hand, learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the petitioner.
However he has admitted that it is a matter in parity with other cases in which other co-accused persons have been granted bail.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, materials available against the petitioner and in view of custody period of the petitioner, I am inclined to release the petitioners on regular bail.
Accordingly, the petitioner named above is directed to be released on bail on furnishing of bail bond Naimuddin Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand ...

Case No. 15 of 2024 subject to the conditions:-

(1) Petitioner shall remain physically present on each and every date till the conclusion of the trial of this case unless prevented from sufficient cause to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court.
(2) Petitioner shall not indulge in any or other similar offence till the conclusion of the trial.
(3) Petitioner shall not indulge in tampering with the prosecution evidences or influencing the prosecution witnesses.
